Mr. Khaled Hamid Chowdhury, Advocate ------- For the Defendant No.2-petitioner
Mr. A.K. Rashedul Huq, Advocate. ------- For the opposite party No.1
Mr. Mahfujur Rahman Roman, Advocate ------- For the opposite party No.5
Ms. Nasima Akhter, Advocate ------- For the opposite party Nos. 3-4&6
parties:
Mrs. Afsana Barik Malik. ------- Defendant No.2-petitioner.
Vs.
Zakaria Hossain Chowdhury and others ------- Plaintiff-opposite parties.
full_judgment:
Sheikh Abdul Awal, J: This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the impugned order dated 09.01.2022 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 4th Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 570 of 2018 rejecting the petitioner’s application under Order VII, Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure for rejection of the plaint should not be set-aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. The brief fact relevant for disposal of this Rule is that the opposite party No.1, Zakaria Hossain Chowdhury as plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 570 of 2018 in the Court of the learned Joint District Judge, 4th Court, Dhaka praying the following reliefs: 
a) Pass a decree that the Plaintiff has title to the 1,00,000 shares (originally 10,000 shares of BDT 100 each that were converted to 1,00,000 shares of BDT 10 each as per Bangladesh Securities and Exchange Commission's order No. SEC/CMRRCD/2009-193/109 dated 15.09.2011) registered in the name of the defendant No.2 and 1,00,000 shares (originally shares of BDT 100 each that were converted to 1,00,000 shares of BDT 10 each as per Bangladesh Securities and Exchange Commission's Order No. SEC/CMRRCD/2009-193/109 dated 15.09.2011) registered in the name of Mrs. Roksana Islam (the predecessor of Defendant Nos. 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6) in the share registered of Defendant No.1 Bank and any right shares, bonus shares and dividend arising there from calculated from the date of the agreement for Amicable Partition dated 25.06.1999 till date; 
b) Pass a decree directing the Defendant No.1 Bank of rectify its share register and insert the name of the Plaintiff in the place of Defendant No.2 and Mrs. Ruksana Islam (predecessor of Defendant Nos. 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6) in connection with the 1,00,000 shares (originally 10,000 shares of BDT 100 each that were converted to 1,00,000 shares of BDT 10 each as per Bangladesh securities and Exchange Commission's Order No. SEC/CMRRCD/2009-193/109 dated 15.09.2011 registered in the name of the Defendant no.2 and 1,00,000 shares (originally 10,000 shares of BDT 100 each that were converted to 1,00,000 shares of BDT 10 each as per Bangladesh Securities and Exchange Commission's Order No. SEC/CMRRCD/2009-193/109 dated 15.09.2011) registered in the name of Mrs. Roksana Islam (The predecessor of Defendant Nos. 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6) and any right shares, bonus shares and divided arising therefore calculated from the date of the Agreement for Amicable Partition dated 24.06.1999 till date; 
c) Award cost against the Defendant and in favour of the Plaintiff; and 
d) Award such other or further relief or reliefs as the plaintiff may be entitled to in law and equity.

3. Defendants entered appearance in the suit and filed written statements denying all the material allegations made in the plaint contending, inter-alia, that the suit is not maintainable in its present form and manner, the suit is parred by limitation, the plaintiff filed the suit on false averments, the contents of the plaint do not disclose any cause of action of the suit and as such, the suit is liable to be dismissed.

4. In this backdrop, while the suit was in progress the defendants filed an application under Order VII, Rule 11 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for rejection of the plaint stating, interalia, that the contents of the plaint do not disclose any cause of action of the suit, the suit is barred by limitation, the plaintiff earlier over the self-same subject matter filed Title Suit No. 420 of 2004 for declaration of title and thereafter having realized the difficulties the plaintiff filed an application for withdrawal of the suit with a permission to sue afresh which was allowed on 02.10.2005 and thereafter, the plaintiff long lapses of 14 years over the self-same subject matter filed the present suit praying similar type of reliefs which is clearly barred by the principle of res-judicature, the ultimate result of the suit is as clear as daylight such a suit should be buried at its inception so that no further time is consumed in a fruitless litigation. The subject matter of the instant suit is clearly and completely company matter and a case being Company Matter No. 112 of 2005 had filed by the present plaintiff which was also disallowed by judgment and order dated 31.05.2018 passed by a Company Bench of this Court and as such, at any rate the plaint of the suit is liable to be rejected to secure the ends of justice.

5. The learned Joint District Judge, 4th Court, Dhaka after hearing the application by his order No. 31 dated 09.01.2022 rejected the application holding that the subject matter of the suit based on bundle of facts which can be decided only at the trial on taking evidence.

6. Aggrieved thereby the present defendant No.2-petitioner, Mrs. Afsana Barik Malik preferred this revision application and obtained the present Rule.

7. Mr. Khaled Hamid Chowdhury, the learned Advocate appearing for the defendant No.2-petitioner in the course of argument takes us through the plaint of the suit and other materials on record including the application under Order VII, Rule 11 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure and then submits that the contents of the plaint do not disclose any cause of action for the suit which totally disclosed a company case and it is on record that a company bench of this Court earlier after a detailed hearing of both the sides by its judgment and order dated 31.05.2018 disallowed the Company Matter being No. 112 of 2005 and thereafter, the litigant plaintiff with ill motive filed the instant civil suit to get illegal benefit from family dispute. He further submits that the suit is plainly barred by limitation as it is on record that the plaintiff at first instance withdrawn the suit on 02.10.2005 with permission to sue afresh and thereafter long lapse of 14 years the plaintiff filed the present suit on the self-same subject matter. The learned Advocate further referring the judgment of a Company Bench of this Court submits that earlier over the self-same matter a Company Bench of this Court decided the matter by judgment and order dated 31.05.2018 passed in Company Matter No. 112 of 2005 and against that judgment the plaintiff filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1012 of 2019 before the Hon’ble Appellate Division of Bangladesh Supreme Court and the said Civil Petition having been dismissed for non-prosecution and the present plaintiff after being unsuccessful in that company matter up to the Hon’ble Appellate Division filed the instant suit on false averments although the Court below without considering all these material aspects of the case most illegally rejected the application under Order VII, Rule 11 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure by the impugned order, which occasioned a failure of justice. Finally, the learned Advocate submits that the Plaintiff filed Company Matter before Company Bench of High Court being Company Matter 112 of 2005 under the Companies Act, 1994 for rectification of the share register. The said company matter was rejected by Judgment and Order dated 31.05.2018 with the following observation- 
"But so far the allegation as has been brought in the instant application that the respondent No. 1 company has unlawfully denied to register the transfer of the shares so far it concerns to the respondent Nos. 3 and 5, the same has got no merit on the ground that the allegedly submitted from 117 to the respondent No. 6 Bank were inadequate and submission of original share certificates along with non-executed form 117, cannot constitute a valid transfer of shares. But so far the question as to the entitlement of the petitioner to the said shares owned by the respondent Nos. 2 and 4 is concerned, it appears that the respondent No 2 and 4 have already made compromise with the petitioner and accordingly their shares have already been treated as transferred to the petitioner by way of the compromise effected from the date of compromise.”

8. In view of the above findings of the company bench it is clear that the instant suit is a vexatious suit and ultimate result of the suit is as clear as day light, such a suit should be buried at its inception so that no further time is consumed in such a fruitless litigation. The learned Advocate to strengthen his submissions has relied on the decisions reported in 45 DLR(AD) 31, 11 BLD 315, 10 BLT 39, 11 BLD 312, 43 DLR 242, 53 DLR(AD) 12 and 55 DLR 211.

9. Mr. A.K. Rashedul Huq, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party No. 1, on the other hand, supports the impugned order, which was according to him just, correct and proper. The learned Advocate in the course of argument referring plaint of the suit submits that the contents of the plaint do disclose cause of action for the suit, the plea as taken in the application under Order VII, Rule 11 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure is motivated, ill advised and misconceived. The learned Advocate further submits, it is on record that earlier the plaintiff filed Civil Suit No. 420 of 2004 and the said suit was withdrawn by the plaintiff with a permission to sue a fresh and soon thereafter the plaintiff filed a company case before the appropriate company bench of this Court being Company Matter No. 112 of 2005 and the said company case was disallowed with a direction to raise the subject matter before appropriate civil Court and accordingly, the innocent plaintiff filed the present suit for proper relief as per direction of the company bench and as such, there is no legal scope to say that the case is barred by resjudicata or the suit is misconceived one as the subject matter of the suit is company bench matter etc. The learned Advocate further submits that in the attending facts and circumstances, the case is not barred by limitation whatsoever, besides the question of limitation is a mixed question of facts and law which can only be decided at the trial on taking evidence that may be adduced by the parities.

10. Finally, Mr. A.K. Rashedul Huq submits that the present suit is based on a family settlement which was reduced into writing and duly registered on 24.06.1999 under the title of Family Settlement Agreement; there is a good number of documentary evidences which can be substantiated by the oral evidences during trial in favour of the plaintiff-opposite party No.1. The plaintiff also has money receipts and family settlement agreement to prove his case and thus it can safely be said that the suit is not a fruitless litigation.

11. Having heard the learned Advocates for both the sides and having gone through the materials on record including the impugned order and the application filed under Order VII, Rule 11 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the only question that falls for our consideration in this civil Revision whether the learned Joint District Judge, 4th Court, Dhaka committed any error in rejecting the application under Order VII, Rule 11 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure by the impugned order on the ground that the questions raised could only be decided on proper issues at the time of hearing of the suit.

12. Firstly, the learned Advocate for the defendant petitioner argues that the suit is barred by limitation, in the facts and circumstances of the case the plaintiff is not entitled to get benefit of section 14 of the Limitation Act as the suit is clearly time barred being the long gap of more than 14 years.

13. It is true that section 14 of the Limitation Act contain the provision to extension of the period of limitation. In this case we have already indicated that the plaintiff earlier filed Title Suit No. 420 of 2004 before the Assistant Judge, Dhaka and thereafter they filed an application to withdraw the suit with liberty to sue afresh and the said application was allowed and soon thereafter, the plaintiff filed Company matter before the Company Bench of this Court being Company Matter No. 112 of 2005 and after hearing of both the sides the company bench disallowed the Company Matter No. 112 of 2005 by its judgment dated 31.05.2018 with a direction that “the disputed question of title to the properties involved in the said issue and as such the question of part performance by the parties under the Family Settlement Agreement dated 24.6.1999 is required to be considered upon evidence in a properly constituted suit for specific performance of contract." And, soon thereafter finding no other way the present plaintiff-opposite party filed the instant Title Suit No. 570 of 2018 impleading the defendant petitioner and others praying the reliefs as quoted above.

14. Therefore, in the facts and circumstances of the case in a suit of this nature, we are constrained to hold that the suit is not barred by limitation. Moreover, the proposition of law by now well settled that the question of limitation in a suit is a mixed question of law and fact which can be decided only at the trial on taking evidence. Therefore, the argument as advanced by the learned Advocate that the suit is barred by limitation falls to the ground.

15. Secondly, the learned Advocate for the petitioner argues with force that the suit is a fruitless litigation and the contents of the plaint do not disclose any cause of action for the suit.

16. To meet this branch of argument, we have carefully studied the contents of the plaint to the best of our ability and it appears to us that the contents of the plaint do disclose the cause of action for the suit. Moreover, in this case the learned Advocate for the plaintiff-opposite party No.1 argues that the plaintiff filed the suit based on a family settlement which was reduced into writing and duly registered on 24.06.1999 under the title of Family Settlement Agreement. There are good number of documentary evidences which can be substantiated by the oral evidences during trial in favour of the plaintiff-opposite party No.1, the plaintiff also has money receipts and family settlement agreement to prove his case. Therefore, in the above facts and circumstances of the case, we are unable to see eye to eye to such submission of the learned Advocate for the defendant petitioner that the suit is a fruitless litigation and the contents of the plaint do not disclose any cause of action for the suit.

17. Another contention raised by the learned Advocate Mr. Khaled Hamid Chowdhury for the defendant No. 1, petitioner that the subject matter of the case is absolutely company matter and over the self same issue company matter has already been disposed of finally and thus, the instant suit is hopelessly barred by the principle of resjudicata.

18. It is true that the subject matter of the case is more or less company bench matter and accordingly, the plaintiff as applicant earlier filed a company matter being No. 112 of 2005 before a appropriate company bench of this Court which was disallowed by judgment and order dated 31.05.2018 with observation that- “But so far the question of entitlement of the petitioner to the transfer of shares held in the name of the respondent Nos. 3 and 5 are concerned, it appears that the disputed question of title to the property is involved in the said issue and as such the question of part performance by the parties under the Family Settlement Agreement dated 24.06.1999 is required to be considered upon evidence in a properly constituted suit for specific performance of contract”

19. In view of the above, particularly in the facts and circumstances of the case, we are unable to agree with the submissions of the learned Advocate for the defendant No. 1, petitioner that the subject matter of the suit is company bench matter and the instant suit is misconceived and the suit is hopelessly barred by the principle of resjudicata. Besides, questions of limitation and resjudicata raised in the application for rejecting the plaint are mixed questions of law and fact which need thorough investigation on adequate evidence for arriving at a correct decision on framing specific issues by the trial Court. We, therefore, find no merit in the contention. The decisions cited are distinguishable on facts.

20. By now we have covered the points raised by the learned Advocate Mr. Khaled Hamid Chowdhury for the defendant No. 1, petitioner.

21. In view of our discussions made in the foregoing paragraphs it is by now clear that the instant Rule must fail.

22. In the result, the Rule is discharged. In the facts and circumstances of the case there will be no order as to costs.

23. Since the matter is an old one of 2004, the trial Court below is directed to dispose of the suit expeditiously as early as possible preferably within 6 months from the date of receipt of this judgment.

Let a copy of this judgment be communicated to the Court concerned at once.

End.

lawyer:
Surojit Bhattacharjee with Farhana Siraj Ronnie, Advocate—For the Petitioners in both Civil Revisions. 
Subrata Chowdhury with Rabin Chandra Paul, Advocate—For the Opposite-parties in both Civil Revision.
parties:
Shree Shree Radha Gobinda Jew Bigraha, Hasanpara (Bazarhat), Dhaperhat and another ------ Petitioner
vs
Shree Pravat Chandra Adhikary and anothers ------ Opposite-Parties
full_judgment:
The Rules issued in Civil Revision No. 435 of 2008 and Civil Revision No. 436 of 2008 having involved similar questions of facts and law are taken up together for disposal by this single judgment. 

2. In Civil Revision No. 435 of 2008, the Rule was issued calling upon opposite party Nos.1-4 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 24-9-2007 (decree signed on 1-10-2007) passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Gaibandha in Other Appeal No.165 of 2006, affirming the judgment and decree dated 11-10-2006 (decree signed on 17-10-2006) passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Sadullahpur, Gaibandha in Other Suit No.49 of 2003, dismissing' the suit should not be set-aside and/or why such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper, shall not be passed. 

3. In Civil Revision No. 436 of 2008, the Rule was issued calling upon opposite party Nos.1-2 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 24-9-2007 (decree signed on 1-10-2007) passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Gaibandha in Other Class Appeal No.164 of 2006 (heard and disposed of analogously with Other Class Appeal No.165 of 2006), affirming the judgment and decree dated 11-10-2006 (decree signed on 17-10-2006) passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Sadullahpur, Gaibandha in Other Class Suit No.110 of 2002 (heard and disposed of analogously with Other Class Suit No. 49 of 2003), decreeing the suit should not be set-aside and/or why such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper, shall not be passed. Pending the hearing of both the Rules, the parties were directed to maintain the status quo regarding the possession and position of the suit land. 

4. The petitioner Shree Shree Radha Gobinda Jew Bigraha, represented by Shree Dulal Chandra Saha, President of Shree Shree Radha Gobinda Jew Bigraha Managing Committee as plaintiff instituted Other Class Suit No.49 of 2003 in the Court of the learned Assistant Judge, Sadullahpur, Gaibandha for declaration of title and also for a declaration that Deeds of Gift Nos.6704 of 1996 and 1657 of 1998 executed and registered by defendant Nos.2 and 3 in favour of defendant No.4 are collusive and thereby, the title of the plaintiffs has not been affected. 

5. The plaintiffs' case, in short, is that before immemorial time, Shree Shree Radha Gobinda Jew Deity was installed on the land of CS Khatian Nos. 175 and 176 and after the promulgation of permanent settlement the said property came under the Zamindari of Raja Mahendra Ranjan Roy Chowdhury and the said Zamindar was appointed Sebait. The homestead of Mahendra Ranjan was far from the Deity for which Puma Chandra Adhikary was appointed Pujari. Accordingly, CS Khatian was prepared and published in the name of Pujari Puma Chandra Adhikary under Sebait Raja Mahendra Ranjan Roy Chowdhury. A total of 1.19 acres of land is Debutter property but not private property and there is no personal right, interest or possession over the suit property. The temple is situated on plot No.70, which was used and enjoyed by the Hindu people at large and the usufructs of the other lands are used for the Puja of the Deity. Pujari Puma Chandra Adhikary was permitted to live in 05 decimals of the land of plot No.69, Pujari Puma Chandra Adhikary subsequently left the temple premises for the village Kadimnagar and was appointed Sebait of Shree Shree Gopal Giridhary Jew Deity in the said village Kadimnagar and defendant Nos.1-3 were born therein. In the meantime, the local people carried out the Puja of the Deity in suit through various pujaris. But subsequently, defendant No.1 came back, and the Puja Committee again appointed him Pujari and he used to live in the said 05 decimals of the land of plot No.69, The Government acquired 08 decimals of land from plot No.69 while the plaintiff erected 10 shops on the rest 09 decimals of land of the said plot No.69 and rented it to various persons by which the expenditure of the puja is met up. The SA record was wrongly prepared and published in the name of Pujari Puma Chandra Adhikari and because of that wrong record, the defendants illegally created Deed of Gift Nos. 6704 and 1657 dated 16-11-1996 and 25-2-1998 respectively in favour of the Deity and defendant No.4. By the said wrong records-of-rights and illegal Deeds of Gift, the title of the plaintiff has been clouded and hence the suit. 

6. Defendant Nos.1-4 contested the said suit by filing a written statement denying the material averments made in the plaint and contending inter alia, that the suit property belonged to Raja Mahendra Ranjan Roy Chowdhury. He appointed Puma Chandra Adhikary as the 'Purohit' in his house. As the consideration for his religious service Raja Mahendra Ranjan gave him nishkar pattan of 1.19 acres of land of CS Khatian No.176 for permanently residing therein as well as for maintenance of his livelihood. Accordingly, the said land described in Schedule 'Kha' was recorded in his name in CS Khatian No.176. He possessed 22 decimals of the land of Plot No.69 by making a homestead thereon, by performing religious rites towards the Deity established in the land of Plot No.70 and by cultivating 91 decimals of the land of Plot No.67. RS Khatian No.188 was duly published in his name. At the request of the people in general belonging to the Hindu Religion, Puma Chandra dedicated, by registered Deed of Gift No.6704 dated 6-11-1996, 32 decimals of land from Plot No.67 and 52 decimals from Plot No.91 to the Radha-Gobinda Deity. He died leaving behind his three sons namely, Prabhat, Ashutosh and Shachin. Shachin and Ashutosh gifted their share to defendant No.4 by registered Deed of Gift No.1657 dated 25-2-1998. The defendants have title and possession over the 'Ka' schedule land. The defendants have been possessing the shops established in the suit land and also filed Other Suit No.110 of 2002 for a decree of permanent injunction as the plaintiff threatened to forcibly dispossess them from the suit property. The plaintiff has no title and possession in the suit land and hence, the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

7. Both Other Suit No.49 of 2003 and Other Suit No.110 of 2002 were heard analogously. 

8. During the trial, the plaintiff examined 6(six) witnesses and produced some documents, which were marked as exhibits 1-12. On the other hand, the defendants adduced 2(two) witnesses and produced some documents which were marked as exhibits L-U. 

9. After hearing both the parties, the trial Court by separate judgments and decrees dated 10-11-2006 (decrees signed on 17-10-2006) dismissed Other Suit No.49.of 2033 and decreed Other Suit No.110 of 2002. 

10. Against the judgment and decree of the trial Court passed in Other Suit No.49 of 2003, the plaintiff preferred Other Appeal No.165 of 2006 while, against the judgment and decree of the trial Court passed in Other Suit No.110 of 2002 preferred Other Appeal No.164 of 2006 in the Court of the learned District Judge, Gaibandha. Both the appeals were transferred to the 1st Court of Joint District Judge, Gaibandha for their disposal. 

11. However, again the Appellate Court heard both the appeals analogously but, by the separate judgments and decrees dated 24-9-2007 (decrees signed on 1-10-2007) dismissed both the appeals. 

12. Against the judgment and decree of the Court of Appeal below, the plaintiff as petitioner filed Civil Revision No.435 of 2008 and the same plaintiff as defendant-petitioner filed Civil Revision No.436 of 2008 and obtained the respective Rules and the orders of status quo in respect of possession and position in the suit land till the disposal of the Rules. 

13. Having placed the Civil Revision, Mr. Surojit Bhattacharjee along with Ms. Farhana Siraj Ronnie, learned Advocate for the petitioner in both the Civil Revisions submits that both the Courts below concurrently erred in law and facts as to that as per CS Khatian No.176, admittedly the suit property along with the entire property appertaining to that CS Khatian No.176 belonged to the Deity, Shree Shree Radha Gobinda Jew Bigraha and the predecessor of the defendants in Other Suit No.49 of 2003 and the plaintiffs of Other Class Suit No.110 of 2002 was the Purohit of the Deity and, as such„ they cannot claim the property as the personal property of their predecessor. Both the Courts below again concurrently committed errors of law resulting in errors in the decision occasioning failure of justice by failing to consider that once the Debutter property, it cannot be claimed as personal property and, as such„ the subsequent records-of-rights such as SA and BRS Khatian prepared in their names have no legal basis and similarly, the subsequent transfer based on such wrong recording has also no legal effect. 

14. On the other hand, Mr. Subrata Chowdhury along with Mr. Rabin Chandra Paul, learned Advocate for the opposite parties in both the Civil Revisions submits that as per the CS Khatian No.176, the property was under the control and management of the Courts of Wards and the predecessor of the opposite parties were tenant as Chakran Purohit. Accordingly, both the Courts below rightly found title in favour of the predecessor of the opposite parties as well as in favour of the opposite parties themselves and thus, there being no legal infirmity in the concurrent findings and observations of the Courts below, both the Rules are liable to be discharged. The learned Advocate for the opposite parties further submits that since the predecessor of the opposite parties acquired title based on the CS Khatian, the property was rightly recorded in the SA and BRS Khatian in their names and accordingly, they had also the transferable interest by executing the said Deed of No.1657 dated 25-2-1998 and thus, again there being no legal infirmity and illegality in the concurrent findings and observations of both the Courts below, both the Rules are liable to be discharged. 

15. I have perused both the Civil Revisions along with the records of the Courts below and heard the learned Advocates from both sides. 

16. It appears that both the parties claimed their respective titles based on CS Khatian No.176, which has been marked as exhibit 1(Ka) on behalf of the plaintiff of Other Suit No.49 of 2003 and as exhibit 'Ka' on behalf of the plaintiff of Other Suit No.110 of 2002. The plaintiff of Other Suit No.49 of 2003 also submitted CS Khatian No.175, which has been marked as exhibit 1. As per the case of the plaintiff of Other Suit No.49 of 2003 and defendants of Other Class Suit No.110 of 2002, the entire properties appertaining to CS Khatian Nos. 175 and 176 belonged to the Deity namely, Shree Shree Radha Gobinda Jew Bigrah, which was within the zamindari of Raja Mahendra Ranjan Roy Chowdhury, and he appointed himself as the Sebait of the Deity. As per CS Khatian No.176, the Sebait of the Deity was the superior landlord and the name of the predecessor of the defendants of Other Suit No.49 of 2003 and plaintiff of Other Class Suit No.110 of 2002 was recorded as the Purohit of the Deity and, as such, no personal title was created in favour of the predecessor of the opposite parties. On the other hand, it is the case of the opposite parties that their predecessor was the Chakran Purohit of 1.19 acres of land appertaining to CS Khatian No.176 and, as such, he acquired personal title therein. Both the Courts below found that the property personally belonged to the predecessor of the opposite parties. 

17. I have meticulously perused and analysed the said CS Khatian Nos. 175 and 176. It appears from CS Khatian No.175 that the superior landlord of the land measuring 1.19 acres appertained thereto was the Court of Wards for Raja Mahendra Ranjan Roy Chowdhury MBE, and it was debutter property and the tenant in possession was also the Court of Wards for Raja Mahendra Ranjan Roy Chowdhury, Sebait of Radha Gobinda Jew Bigrah. It further appears from the 2nd page of CS Khatian No.175 that CS Khatian No.176 was prepared under CS Khatian No.175. Similarly, it appears from CS Khatian No.176 that the superior landlord was the Court of Wards for Raja Mahendra Ranjan Roy Chowdhury MBE, '175 Sebait' and the name of Puma Chandra Adhikary, the predecessor of opposite parties was recorded as the 'Chakran Purohit in possession. The words '175 Sebait' that appeared in CS Khatian No.176 contemplate that the Sebait mentioned in CS Khatian No.175 was also the Sebait or continued to be the same Sebait of the property of CS Khatian No.176 i.e., CS Khatian No.176 was prepared under CS Khatian No.175. Thus, there are only 1.19 acres of land under CS Khatian No. 175 and its Sub-CS Khatian No.176 and the entire property is debutter property. Had the properties of both CS Khatian No.175 and its sub-Khaitan No.176 belonged to Raja Mahendra and had he installed the Deity therein, the said properties might have not been recorded in the name of the Court of Wards in the said two CS Khatians. In this regard, the learned Advocate for the opposite parties also submits that as per the CS Khatians, the said properties were under the control and management of the Court of Wards and Zamindar Raja Mahendra was Sebait thereof. So, I find substance in the pleadings and submissions made in this regard by the petitioner that before immemorial time, Shree Shree Radha Gobinda Jew Bigraha was installed on the land of CS Khatian Nos. 175 and 176 and after the promulgation of permanent settlement the said property came under the Zamindari of Raja Mahendra Ranjan Roy Chowdhury and the said Zamindar was appointed Sebait. 

18. But it is the case of the defendant-opposite parties that Puma Chandra Adhikary, their predecessor was the 'Purohit' of Zamindar Raja Mahendra and as the consideration of his religious service, the Zamindar gave him 'niskar pattan' of 1.90 acres of land of CS Khatian No.176 for permanently residing therein and maintenance of his livelihood. It is their further case that at the request of the local people, in general, belonging to the Hindu Religion, he dedicated by registered Deed of Gift No.6704 dated 6-11-1996 in total 84 decimals of land to the Radha-Gobinda Jew Bigraha. Thus, from the case of the defendant-opposite parties, it appears that the suit property was beyond the debutter property. But it has already been found that the entire property of CS Khatian No.175 and its Sub-Khatian No.176 is debutter property. At this stage, the learned Advocate for the opposite parties submits that as per the CS Khatians, the property was under the control and management of Courts of Wards and not under the control and management of the Sebait and the predecessor of the opposite parties was a Chakran Purohit under the Courts of Wards. However, they could not produce any evidence to prove that they were ever tenant under the Court of Wards. Moreover, as per sections 6 and 7 of the Courts of Wards Act, 1879, no Debutter property can be claimed by any Court of Wards. However, the Court of Wards also claimed on behalf of the Deity. 

19. Therefore, it appears that the entire property of CS Khatian No.175 and its Sub-Khatian No.176 belonged to the Deity represented by its Sebait. Moreover, it is admitted by both parties that in the suit premises, the Deity namely Shree Shree Radha Gobinda Jew Bigraha is situated. Therefore, the Sebaitwas the Sebait of the Deity of Shree Shree Radha Gobinda Jew Bigraha. Accordingly, as per the CS Khatians, the predecessor of the opposite parties was a tenant under the Deity without any rent. Moreover, from the remarking column of the CS Khatian, it appears that Puma Chandra Adhikary, the predecessor of the opposite parties was in the possession of the property as Chakran Purohit i.e. in his official capacity and not personal capacity. Accordingly, so long he was in the office of the Purohit, he was entitled to possess and enjoy the said property. Moreover, it appears from the pleadings of both parties that by Deed of Gift No.6704 dated 6-11-1996, the opposite parties gifted the property to the Deity. However, the plaintiff did not accept the deed rather, claimed that the opposite parties had no legal right to make such a gift.It appears from both Sub-CS Khatian No.176 and SA Khatian No.188 that 32 decimals of land of Plot No.67 were jungle, 22 decimals of Plot No.69 were homesteads consisting of five houses, 13 decimals of Plot No.70 were Mandir (Debosthan)consisting of 04 houses and 52 decimals of Plot No.91 were for public usage. Thus, the entire property was debutter property. Therefore, gifting the debutter property to the same 'Debata' i.e., the Deity was nothing but an attempt to establish their title in the remaining properties. But except for the property gifted by the opposite parties, there remain only 22 decimals of land in their names. 

20. Now during the hearing, the learned Advocate for the opposite parties candidly submits that factually the opposite parties possess only 07 decimals of land.But, it appears from the deposition of DW 1 that they are no more Purohit of the Deity rather, they are engaged in the photo framing business. Thus, they cannot claim any portion of the debutter property in the capacity of purohit. The Sebait also cannot transfer any debutter property. On these points, in the case of Bangladesh vs Abdul Hye and others, 24 BLT (AD) 340 the Appellate Division held that a 'Poojari' is a servant of the Sebait, and no part of the rights and obligations of the latter are transferrable to him. When the appointment of a 'Purohit' has been at the will of the founder, the mere fact that the appointee has performed the worship for several generations will not confer an independent right upon the members of the family so appointed and will not entitle them as of right to be continued in office as priests. Thus, the suit property was not transferrable by the Sebait in favour of Puma Chandra predecessor of the defendants nor can they claim any title in the suit property as of right as the sons of the then 'Purohit'. Both the Courts below failed to consider that the Debutter property cannot be claimed as personal property by any person whatever might be his status. Accordingly, both the Courts below also failed to appreciate that the subsequent SA and BRS records prepared in the names of the opposite parties, or their predecessor have no legal basis inasmuch as the entire property being debutter property without any reservation, the same is beyond the scope and application of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 as per section 20(5)(ii)(c) thereof and accordingly, nobody can claim any tenancy right in the debutter property under the Government. 

21. Since the entire property of Sub-CS Khatian No.175 belonged to the Deity, the Purohit thereof cannot claim the property as his personal property. Accordingly, the transfer deed bearing No.1657 dated 25-2-1998 transferring some portion of the debutter property had also no legal basis and implication and thereby, no title has been transferred to the transferee thereof. 

22. In such facts and circumstances, I find substance in the submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioner in both the Civil Revisions. 

23. It transpires from the discussions, findings and observations made above that both the Courts below committed gross errors of law resulting in errors in the decision occasioning failure of justice having not considered that the entire property appertaining to CS Khatian No.175 and its Sub-Khatian No.176 is Debutter property and no one whatever might his status can claim the same as his personal property. Hence, I find merit in both the Rules. 

24. Accordingly, both the Rules are made absolute without any costs. 

25. Therefore, the impugned judgments and decrees passed by the Courts below are set-aside. Other Class Suit No.49 of 2003 instituted in the Court of Assistant Judge, Sadullahpur, Gaibandha is hereby decreed as prayed for and Other Class Suit No.110 of 2002 filed in the same Court of Assistant Judge, Sadullahpur, Gaibandha is dismissed without any order as to costs. 

Send down the records of the Courts below at once. 

End.

full_judgment:
Md Khasruzzmaman, J: In the application under Article 102(2)(a)(ii) of the Constitution, on 15-12-2021 the Rule Nisi under adjudication was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the judgment and order dated 25-9-2021 passed by the Member No.1, Land Appeal Board in Appeal No.5-84 of 2020 (Nam:) summarily dismissing the appeal in admission hearing and thereby affirming the judgments and orders dated 6-11-2019, 14-11-2018 and 18-3-2018 passed by the respondent Nos. 3, 5 and 6 in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 12 of 2019, in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 6 of 2018 and in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 23 of 2017-18 respectively (Annexure-I) should not be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

2. Facts necessary for disposal of the Rule Nisi, in short, are as follows: 
Md Showkat Ali, Md Dabir Uddin and Md Shomser Ali all sons of late Rofetullah were the original owners of 49 decimals of land appertaining to SA Khatian No.826, SA Plot No.5823. Out of said 49 decimals of land, Md Shomser Ali vide Hiba-bil-iwaz Deed No.11502 dated 25-3-1963 transferred 25 decimals of land to his son Md Jamal Uddin who mutated the same in his name being Holding No.690. It is stated that since Jamal Uddin was minor, land development tax was paid in his father's name up to 1424 BS and he was in possession of the same by constructing house. When Jamal Uddin became ill, the writ petitioner rendered nursing service to him including necessary treatment. Being satisfied with the nursing service rendered by the petitioner, Jamal Uddin transferred the case property to the writ petitioner vide Hiba-bil-iwaz Deed No. 8097 dated 22-11-2017. The petitioner mutated the case property in his name by opening separate Holding No.5564 vide Mutation Case No.1018/17-18. Thereafter, on 31-1-2018 respondent Nos. 7 to 10 as petitioners filed Miscellaneous Case No. 23 of 2017-2018 before the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Nilphamari, District-Nilphamari for cancellation of writ petitioner's Mutation Case No.1018 of 2017-18 on the ground that he got the case property mutated in his name by creating false and forged documents vide Annexure-B to the writ petition. On the basis of the allegation, the Assistant Commissioner (Land) issued letter dated 20-2-2018 to the District Registrar, Rangpur requesting him to send a report as to the genuineness of the Hiba-bil-iwaz Deed No.11502 dated 25-3-1963. Accordingly, on 4-3-2018 the Sub-Registrar, Sadar, Rangpur sent a report stating that the alleged deed was rightly registered on 25-3-1963 but the concerned page of the volume being torn and damaged, information regarding the parties to the deed, mouza, area of land, khatian and plot number could not be possible to supply vide Annexures-C and C-1 to the writ petition. Thereafter, Jamal Uddin who has gifted the suit property to the writ petitioner filed an application before the Sub Registrar, Sadar, Rangpur asking information about the Hiba-bil-iwaz Deed No.11502 dated 25-3-1963 whereupon the Sub-Registrar, Sadar, Rangpur vide his report dated 4-4-2018 informed that the alleged deed was rightly registered on 25-3-1963 but due to the concerned page of the volume being torn and damaged information as prayed for could not be supplied vide Annexure-D to the writ petition. 

3. Having considered the application filed by the respondent Nos.7 to 10 together with the allegation and reports submitted by the concerned registration office, the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Nilphamari Sadar, Nilphamari vide his order dated 18-3-2018 cancelled the mutation of the writ petitioner vide Annexure-F to the writ petition. 

4. Against the aforesaid order dated 18-3-2018 passed by the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Nilphamari Sadar, Nilphamari in Nam Miscellaneous Case No.23 of 2017-18, writ petitioner filed Miscellaneous Appeal No.06 of 2018 before the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Nilphamari for redress. After hearing the parties and on perusal of the materials on record and the report dated 28-9-2018 submitted by the District Registrar, Nilphamari, vide his order dated 14-11-2018 dismissed the appeal by affirming the order dated 18-3-2018 passed by the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Nilphamari Sadar, Nilphamari (Annexure-G-1). 

5. Against the aforesaid order dated 14-11-2018 passed by the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 6 of 2018, the writ petitioner filed Appeal Case No. 12 of 2019 before the Additional Divisional Commissioner, Rangpur. After hearing the parties and on perusal of the materials on record, the Additional Divisional Commissioner, Rangpur vide his order dated 6-11-2019 dismissed the appeal by affirming the order dated 14-11-2018 passed by the Additional Deputy Commissioner, Nilphamari in Miscellaneous Appeal No.6 of 2018 (Annexure-H). 

6. Against the aforesaid order dated 6-11-2019 passed by the Additional Divisional Commissioner(Revenue), Rangpur in Appeal Case No. 12 of 2019, the writ petitioner filed Appeal Case No.5-84 of 2020(Nam:) before the Land Appeal Board. Upon hearing the parties on the admissibility of the appeal, the Member-1, Land Appeal Board vide his order dated 25-9-2021 dismissed the appeal (Annexure-I). 

7. Challenging the said order dated 25-9-2021 passed by the Member-1, Land Appeal Board, Segunbagicha, Dhaka, the writ petitioner filed the instant writ petition and obtained the Rule Nisi. 

8. Respondent Nos. 7-10 filed affidavit-in-opposition and two supplementary affidavits-in-opposition denying the materials allegations made in the writ petition. The case of the respondent Nos. 7 to 10 as stated in the affidavit-in-opposition and supplementary affidavits-in-opposition that their father Nasim Uddin purchased the land from Abdul Karim, Hajor Bibi and another by deed Nos. 9055 dated 27-12-1967 and 6145 dated 17-9-1967 respectively. The land has been duly mutated in the name of their father vide Mutation Case No. 596/79-80 dated 29-9-1980. Subsequently, Nasim Uddin transferred the land in favour of his four daughters i.e. respondent Nos. 7 to 10 vide Hiba-bil-iwaz Deed No. 4404 dated 21-6-2017. They have got the land mutated in their names. It is stated that without cancelling the mutation of the land in favour of the father of the respondent Nos. 7 to 10, the writ petitioner got the land mutated in his name by creating false and forged Deed No. 11502 dated 28-3-1963. The matter of forgery has been admitted by the writ petitioner before the Assistant Commissioner (Land) which was observed concurrently by all the revenue Courts. It is also stated that as per section 6 of the Land Appeal Board Act, 1989 the writ petitioner had an alternative forum of review against the impugned order passed by the. Land Appeal Board. Without exhausting the alternative forum of review the writ petitioner filed the writ petition which is not maintainable in law, It is also stated that the writ petition involves disputed question of title which needs to be adjudicated upon by the Civil Court on taking evidence and the same cannot be possible under the summary procedure under Article 102 of the Constitution and, as such, the Rule Nisi is liable to be discharged. 

9. Mr Md Golam Rossul, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the writ petitioner submits that the date of the alleged deed is 25-3-1963 which is supported by the report dated 29-9-2018 vide Annexure-1 to the supplementary affidavit and, as such, there is no scope to raise any question on the genuineness of the alleged deed No.11502 dated 25-3-1963. But all the revenue Courts failed to appreciate this aspect in cancelling his mutation with regard to the land. Referring to the impugned order he further submits that the impugned order has been passed by a Member of the Land Appeal Board and, as such, the order is corum non judice and hence the same is without jurisdiction. In this respect he has referred a case of Abdul Hakim Gazi (Md) vs Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Land, Dhaka and others, 73 DLR 478. As such, the Rule Nisi is liable to be made absolute. 

10. Mr ABM Altaf Hossain, the learned Advocate alongwith Mr Meah Muhmmad Abdullah Zahid and Mr Md Mehadi Hassan the learned Advocates appearing on behalf of the respondent Nos. 7 to 10, submits that the writ petitioner while making submissions before the Assistant Commissioner (Land) admitted that field porcha filed in Mutation Case No. 1018/17-18 was not correct and by practising fraud the writ petitioner got the land mutated in his name by submitting the forged deed No. 11502 dated 25-3-1963. The matter of forgery was concurrently found by all revenue Courts in their observations and, as such, the Assistant Commissioner (Land) did not commit any illegality in cancelling the mutation of the writ petitioner. He further submits that the writ petitioner had an alternative forum of review against the impugned order as contemplated in section 6 of the Land Appeal Board Act, 1989 and since the writ petitioner did not exhaust the alternative forum of review, the writ petition is not maintainable. In support of his submissions he refers a case of Md Mintu Chowdhury vs Khurshid Nayeem and others, 33 BLD (AD) 72. He also submits that the writ petition involves disputed question of fact as to the title of the petitioner. Until and unless the title of the petitioner is determined by a competent Civil Court by taking evidence, no prayer for mutation of the land can be made. Referring to Annexure-VIII to the supplementary affidavit-in-opposition he contends that the writ petitioner has already filed Other Class Suit No. 136 of 2020 in the Court of Senior Assistant judge, Sadar, Nilphamari for permanent injunction over the suit land, and the suit is pending for taking step under section 30 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Since the question of forgery of the alleged deed and the title of the writ petitioner the land are involved in writ petition, those need to be adjudicated by the competent Civil Court and, as such, the Rule Nisi is liable to be discharged. 

11. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocates for both the parties and perused the writ petition, supplementary affidavit, affidavit-in-opposition, supplementary affidavits-in-opposition and connected documents annexed thereto. 

12. In short the case of the writ petitioner is that he got the land gifted by Md Jamal Uddin vide Hiba-bil-iwaz Deed No. 8097 dated 22-11-2017. The transferor of the writ petitioner Md Jamal Uddin got the land from his father vide Hiba-bil-iwaz Deed No. 11502 dated 25-3-1963, and he mutated the same in his name being Holding No.690. The writ petitioner on the basis of the aforesaid two deeds got the land mutated in his name vide Mutation Case No.1018 of 2017-18, and thereafter he paid the rent to the government up to 1424 13S. 

13. On the other hand, in short the case of the writ respondent Nos. 7 to 10 is that their father namely-Nasim Uddin purchased the land from Abdul Karim, and Hajor Bibi and another vide two Sale Deed Nos. 9055 dated 27-12-1967 and 6145 dated 17-9-1967. Sub-sequently, their father Nasim Uddin got the land mutated in his name vide Mutation Case No.596 of 1979-80. Thereafter, Nasim Uddin transferred the land in favour of the respondent Nos. 7 to 10 by a Hiba-bil-iwaz Deed No. 4404 dated 21-6-2017 and they also mutated their names accordingly. 

14. After coming to know that the writ petitioner got the land mutated in his name vide Mutation Case No. 1018 of 2017-18, the respondent Nos. 7 to 10 raised objection against the mutation of the writ petitioner by filing Miscellaneous Case No. 23 of 2017-18 on the ground of forgery practised by the writ petitioner by obtaining the mutation of the land in his name. The Assistant Commissioner (Land) called for the report from the District Registrar, Rangpur and Assistant Settlement Officer. Having considered the reports and on careful examination of the papers came to a finding that the papers and documents filed by the applicant (writ petitioner) in Mutation Case No.1018 of 2017-18 were fake and forged. He also observed that the applicant (writ petitioner) admitted that the Field Porcha of Mutation Case No. 1018 of 2017-18 was not correct. Consequently, the mutation of the writ petitioner was cancelled vide order dated 18-3-2018 (Annexure-F). 

15. The Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Nilphamari also called for the report from the District Registrar who vide Memo No.349 dated 28-9-2018 sent report to the Additional Deputy commissioner, Nilphamari. On examination of the report the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) came to a definite finding that the alleged deed was registered on 28-3-1963 and the parties to the alleged deed are different persons. Consequently, the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Nilphamari affirmed the order of cancellation of the mutation of the writ petitioner passed by the Assistant Commissioner (Land) (Annexure-G-1). The Additional Divisional Commissioner (Revenue), Rangpur Division, Rangpur also affirmed the order passed by the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue). All the revenue Courts found the forgery with regard to the Mutation Case No. 1018 of 2017-18. 

16. So, from the facts stated above, it appears that the writ petitioner claimed the land by virtue of Hiba-bil-iwaz Deed Nos. 8097/17 dated 22-11-2017 (Annexure-A) and his vendor Md Jamal Uddin got the land from his father by Hiba bil iwaz Deed No. 11502 dated 25-3-1963. On the other hand, respondent Nos. 7 to 10 claimed the same land by virtue of the registered deeds. To satisfy the allegation of forgery against the writ petitioner, the revenue Courts called for several reports from the registration office and came to a definite finding that the parties to the Hiba-bil-iwaz Deed No. 11502 dated 25-3-1963 are different and not tallied with the information stated by the writ petitioner. 

17. Considering the matter, we are of the view that the question of genuineness of the alleged deeds and title of the land need to be ascertained first before dealing with the mutation of the land. Keeping the matter of mutation of the suit land pending the revenue courts could have asked the parties to settle the question of forgery and title of the land by competent Civil Court but that was not done. Whether the alleged deeds in respect of the particular property is genuine or not and who owned title in the land is a matter for determination by a competent Civil Court on taking evidence, which cannot be decided under the summary procedure of this Court under Article 102 of the Constitution. 

18. So, it is clear that the writ petition is involved with the disputed question of fact. Generally, a disputed question of fact is not investigated in a writ petition because an alternative remedy is available there. Rival claims of property and disputed question of title cannot be the subject-matter of the writ. 

19. Reliance may be made in the case of Shamsunnahar &gam and others vs Mohammad Wahidur Rahman and others, 51 DLR (AD) 232 wherein it has been held: 
"However, extraordinary its powers, a writ court cannot and should not decide any disputed question of fact which requires evidence to be taken for settlement. The principle is well-settled and we have no hesitation therefore in observing that all the findings, orders and observations made by the High Court Division on the question of title and possession of the disputed lands are wholly untenable and uncalled for and the dispute can only be decided one way or the other by a competent Civil Court upon taking evidence." 

20. In the case of Tasmina Chowdhury and 12 others vs Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka and others, 49 DLR 29 it has been held: 
"Relying on the above view we find that disputed question of facts are involved in the instant case. Writ jurisdiction is not the proper forum for seeking remedy." 

21. In the present case, the writ petitioners and the writ respondents both have claimed that they have legal instruments in respect of title of the land, and it is settled principal of law that the revenue court has no jurisdiction to determine or declare a legal instrument as void or illegal. This Division as well the Appellate Division in numerous cases settled the point that where disputed question of facts are involved in a writ petition, the said writ petition shall not be maintained. So, when the situation comes before the revenue court, at the first instance Assistant Commissioner (Land) at the time of mutation should have passed an order of direction to determine title of the land by the competent Civil Court without any delay. 

22. In view of the facts and circumstances as stated above and the decisions relied upon and as cited above, we do not find any merit in the Rule Nisi as well as any substance and force in the submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioner which is liable to be discharged. 

23. In the result, the Rule Nisi is discharged without any order as to costs. 

Communicate the order. 

End.

lawyer:
