full_judgment:
Sayed Jahed Mansur, J: This is an application under Article 102 of the constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh. The petitioner moved this writ petition praying for issuance of a Rule calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why section 6 of the Muslim Family Law Ordinance, 1961 shall not be declared ultra virus having been unconstitutional and is of no legal effect etc. on 5-1-2022. Then the petitioner filed a supplementary affidavit for the modification of the prayer in the main petition and prayed for the issuance of a Rule Nisi in the following terms:—
"Let a Rule Nisi be issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why existing way/process of giving permission of another marriage during subsistence of existing marriage without ensuring equal right between/among the wives being violative with the spirit of constitution should not be declared to have been done without lawful authority and is of no legal effect as to why the guidelines should not be framed in respect of polygamy law in Bangladesh for greater protection of family lives of the citizens of i3angladesh and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this court may seem fit and proper.- 

2. The facts as averred in the affidavit and the supplementary affidavit, containing as many as 1-XXXII grounds, basically have been impugned the legality of "Polygamy" as enacted under section 6 of the Muslim Family Law Ordinance, 1961. It is stated that for Muslim, Polygamy originated from the Holy Quran at Chapter -4, Ayat -3 (4:3). It's versus allowed men to merry "two or three or four" women, but asked them to have a single wife if they "fear" they cannot treat them all with equal fairness. Again Chapter-4, Ayat-129 (4:129) declared it difficult for men to achieve despite their best efforts. The Quranic permission for polygamy is incorporated in the statutory law i.e. section 6 of the Muslim Family Law Ordinance, 1961 but it's conditions and restrictions are kept out of the said statutory law. The provision is silent about the issue of equal treatment and fairness with wife when the number of wife is more than one. The provision authorizes the Arbitration Council constituted by the Chairman and two Representatives of the applicant and the wife or wives, to deal with the matter of polygamy and the decision is not a conclusive one and the same is amenable to revision by an Assistant Judge whose decision is final thereon. Thus the provision stopped the door for aggrieved party before the higher Court which is not tenable in law. The Arbitration Council has no scope of considering the circumstantial issues of women like fear of getting a divorce from the husband etc. The provision is silent as to who will initiate criminal proceeding in the event of violation of section 6 of the law. The permission for polygamy from the Arbitration Council is accorded wholesale as the Council is dominated by male members of the Society. There is no provision to verify the consent of the first wife whether it has been actually accorded or not. The Arbitration Council is a non judicial Council and it cannot ensure justice according to law. The Arbitration Council has no jurisdiction to verify the veracity of the reasons stated in the application. The concept of polygamy involves the question of dower and maintenance for the wife but the Arbitration Council has not been empowered to deal with the legal requirements of marriage rather the issues fall within the exclusive jurisdiction of the Family Court under the Family Courts Ordinance, 1985. It cannot summons witnesses nor can it take oral or documentary evidences for proving or disproving the content of the application submitted to the Arbitration Council. The provision does not clear whether the permission of the existing wife has been taken or not. It is the mandate of the provision that a man who contracts another marriage without the permission of the Arbitration Council shall pay immediately the entire amount of the dower, whether prompt or deferred due to the existing wife or wives but this cannot be punishable provision. Amalgamating dower money with any other issue is not tenable in the eye of law. Thus the process of giving permission of polygamy does not allow women opportunity of fair hearing, interfere with the right to life and right to live with dignity as a citizen of Bangladesh being discriminatory and violative to the spirit of the preamble of the Constitution and the rights guaranteed under the Constitution. Article 27 of the Constitution is a facet of equality of status an opportunity pledged in the preamble to the Constitution and ensures equality before the law and the equal protection of law. But the construction of section 6 describes humiliation and arbitrariness which are against the equal treatment and protection of law thus violates Articles 27 and 28 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh. And as such liable to be declared unlawful and is of no legal effect. These are the sum and substance of the writ petition as narrated in the affidavit and supplementary affidavit. 

3. At the time of hearing, we found no commendable efforts on behalf of the writ petitioner to make out the Rule meaningful citing constitutional or other legal interpretation on the grounds as set forth in the writ petition. 

4. On the other hand the learned Deputy Attorney-Genera] submitted that in the context of existing social set up the Arbitration Council discharging its function without prejudice to equal treatment and fairness in deciding the issue of polygamy. The learned Deputy Attorney-General further submitted to not to disturb the long dated statutory provision on the law of polygamy as the personal law for Muslim of Bangladesh has not been suffered in any manner. 

5. We have heard both sides and went into a great detail covering every aspect of the writ petition with due care and attention. 

6. Before we set out our thought/discussion on the subject of polygamy as enacted in section 6 of the Muslim Family Law Ordinance, 1961 and it's constitutional validity, it would not be unjust or out of context to decide the question whether any public interest is involved in this writ petition or, alternatively whether the writ petition can be treated as a Public Interest Litigation (PIL) as averred by the petitioner as an aggrieved person and to have locus standi to invoke the jurisdiction of the High Court Division under Article 102 of the Constitution. 

7. On a careful examination of Para Nos. 1-8 of the writ petition, it appears that the petitioner as a lawyer with a view to ensuring the fundamental rights to life to the citizen and their greater family lives and to ensure women's dignity and their well being of the whole Bangladesh and their protection of law by impugning the law on polygamy in Bangladesh initiated the proceeding which is undoubtedly connected with the women's rights of public nature and devoid of any personal interest. So the instant writ petition can be treated as Public Interest Litigation (PIL). We find support in the observation made by the Appellate Division in the case of Ekushey Television vs Dr. Chowdhury Mahmood Hasan reported in 55 DLR (AD) 26-
"... The nature of public interest litigation (called P1L hereinafter) is completely different from a traditional case which is adversarial in nature whereas PIL is intended to vindicate rights of the people. In such a case benefit will be derived by a large number of people in contrast to a few." 

8. The question of locus standi as decided by the Appellate Division in the case of Dr. Mohiuddin FArooque vs Bangladesh reported in (1997) 49 DLR (AD) I wherein the Appellate Division held:—
".... When a public injury or public wrong or infraction of a fundamental right affecting an indeterminate number of people is involved it is not necessary, in the scheme of our constitution, that the multitude of individuals who has been collectively wronged or injured or whose collective fundamental rights have been invaded are to invoke the jurisdiction under Article 102 in a multitude of individual writ petitions, each representing his own portion of concern. Insofar as it concerns public wrong or public injury or invasion of fundamental rights of an indeterminate number of people, any member of the public, being a citizen, suffering the common injury or common invasion in common with others or any citizen or an indigenous association, as distinguished from a local component of a foreign organization, espousing that particular cause is a person aggrieved and has the right to invoke the jurisdiction under Article 102." 

9. In this writ petition, the petitioner impugned a section of the legislation (section 6 of the Muslim Family Law Ordinance. 1961) which narrated a procedure for previous permission of the Arbitration Council for the 2nd marriage of a man, during the subsistence of an existing marriage and consequence of such marriage without any permission. Therefore the question of the instance case would be whether the permission of the 2nd, marriage during the subsistence of an existing marriage as impugned section 6 of the Muslim Family Law Ordinance, 1961 is in conflict with the spirit of Constitution. 

10. Now, let us deal with the section 6 of the Muslim Family Law Ordinance, 1961 whether the permission under this section is violative of Articles 27 and 28 cf the Constitution and liable to be declared to have been done without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect and whether any guide lines can be formulated in connection with the Rule. Section 6 of the Muslim Family Law Ordinance, 1961 runs as follows:—
"6. Polygamy-(1) No man, during the subsistence of an existing marriage, shall, except with the previous permission in writing of the Arbitration Council, contract another maniage, nor shall, any such marriage contracted without such permission be registered [under the Muslim Marriages and Divorces (Registration) Act, 1974 (LII of 1974)] 
(2) An application for permission under sub-section (1) shall be submitted to the Chairman in the prescribed manner, together with the prescribed fee, and shall state the reasons for the proposed marriage, and whether the consent of the existing wife or wives has been obtained thereto. 
(3) On receipt of the application under sub- section (2), the Chairman shall ask the applicant and his existing wife or wives each to nominate a representative and the Arbitration Council so constituted may, if satisfied that the proposed marriage is necessary and just, grant, subject to such conditions, if any as may be deemed fit, the permission applied for. 
(4) In deciding the application the Arbitration Council shall record its reasons for the decision, and any party may, in the prescribed manner, within the prescribed period, and on payment of the prescribed fee, prefer an application for revision to the Assistant Judge concerned and his decision shall be final and shall not be called in question in any court. 
(5) Any man who contracts another marriage without the permission of the Arbitration Council shall-
(a) pay immediately the entire amount of the dower, whether prompt or deferred, due to the existing wife or wives, which amount, if not so paid, shall be recoverable as arrears of land revenue; and 
(b) on conviction upon complaint be punishable with simple imprisonment which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to ten thousand Taka or with both." 

11. Rule 14 of the Muslim Family Laws Rules. 1961 is also relevant for polygamy which runs as follows:— 
"14. In considering whether another proposed marriage is just and necessary during the continuance of an existing marriage the Arbitration Council may without prejudice to its general powers to consider what is just and necessary have regard to such circumstances, as the following amongst others:—
Sterility, physical infirmity, physical unfitness for the conjugal relation willful avoidance of a decree for restitution of conjugal rights, or insanity, on the part of an existing wife." 

12. Reading the language of section 6 of the Muslim Family Law Ordinance, 1961, it appears that the section consists of two parts. The 1st part deals with the permission of the Arbitration Council and the 2nd part consequence for non compliance of the 1st part. The 1st part requires-!) an application for permission to the Arbitration Council, II) the reasons of the proposed marriage, III) the consent of the existing wife or wives, IV) whether the proposed marriage is necessary and just (also the reasons stated in Rule 14), V) reasons for the decision of the Arbitration Council either accepting or rejecting the application, VI) revision to Assistant Judge by an aggrieved party. The 2nd part focuses consequences- I) payment of dower money to the existing wife or wives and II) a criminal liability of simple imprisonment for one year or with fine which may extend to Ten thousand taka or with both. 

13. From the language of section 6 of the Muslim Family Law Ordinance. 1961 and Rule 14, it appears that in deciding the question of polygamy the Arbitration Council has authorized to give permission. It is under legal obligation to examine the application for permission to consult with the husband and wife and more particularly the consent of the wife or wives which are very much compatible for taking decision on the question of polygamy. There are also provisions to go for revision in the Court of Assistant Judge on behalf of an aggrieved party for taking redress from a judicial authority. Though the decision on revision is termed as final but the door of the higher Court can be invoked in the writ jurisdiction under the existing legal system of Bangladesh. 

14. On the other hand, the consequences of a marriage without the permission of the Arbitration Council guaranteed the dower money of the wife or wives along with a criminal liability. Payment or realization of dower from the husband is the consequence of marriage and the criminal liability is the consequence of violation of condition precedent i.e. permission of Arbitration Council which ensure the right to dower of the wife or wives and imposition of imprisonment/ fine is the consequence violation of statutory provision which can help to create awareness in the society. It is argued that the provision is silent about who would initiate the criminal proceeding but it is clear from 50 DLR (1998) 559 that the first wife was the complainant of the case. It is natural that during the subsistence of the existing wife (1 wife) if the husband marriages second one, the first wife would be the complainant. 

15. One of the grounds taken before us is that section 494 of the Penal Code prescribed a punishment for 7(seven) years imprisonment for a wife who is charged for plurality of husband (a wife who marriage another man during the life time of the husband) but section 6 only provides 01 year imprisonment for a man who marriage another woman during subsistence of the existing wife without any permission of the Arbitration Council. Under the instant section the man is liable for polygamy which is not prohibited in Islam but under section 494 of the Penal Code the wife is liable for polyandry which is prohibited in Islam. It is the lawmakers who gave their thoughts for determining a larger punishment for polyandry than polygamy. The codification of laws in respect of both the cases clearly shows their nature and impact. One cannot overlap the other. The offences are distinct. No discrimination had been done in enacting the loss on the gender issues. 

16. Another ground in favour of the writ petition is cited that dower and maintenance of the wife are connected with the issue of polygamy which fall within the exclusive jurisdiction of the family court under the Family Courts Ordinance. 1985 but the said ordinance was promulgated subject to the provision of Muslim Family Laws Ordinance, 1961 and the issues connected to polygamy rested in the hands of the Arbitration Council. So the ground cannot sustain. 

17. The main theme of the writ petition is polygamy. It is connected with the Muslim marriage which is subject to the terms of the Muslim Personal Law (Shariat) Application Act, 1937. The concept of polygamy is rooted in the Holy Quran. Surah An-Nisaa Ayat 3 tells about the polygamy which means as follows:—
"If you fear you cannot be equitable to orphan girls (in your charge, or misuse their persons), then many women who are lawful for you, two, three, or four, but if you fear you cannot treat so many with equity, marry only one, or a maid or captive. This is better than being iniquitous". 

18. The verse most commonly associated with the topic of polygamy is verse 3 of Surah 4 An-Nisa (Women). A translation by Abdullah Yusuf Ali as:—
"If you fear that you shall not be able to deal justly with the orphans, Marry women of your choice, Two or three or four; but if you fear that you shall not be able to deal justly (with them), then only one, or (a captive) that your right hands possess, that will be more suitable, to prevent you from doing injustice. (Q.4:3) It is believed these verses were revealed after the Battle of Uhud, so that some (Alia Hogben) argue that these verses have been revealed 'because of Allah's concern for the welfare of women and orphans who were left without husbands and fathers who died fighting for the Prophet and for Islam. Others favoring this interpretation (Sunnipath), point out that the second part of verse Q.4:3 states 'but if ye fear that ye shall not be able to deal justly (with them), then only one, or (captive women) that your right hands possess, that will be more suitable, to prevent you from doing injustice." 

19. The interpretation of the Ayat may find in Bangla as follows:- 
"(৩) এ আয়াতে ইয়াতীম মেয়েদের বৈবাহিক জীবনের অধিকার সংরক্ষণের উপর বিশেষ গুরুত্ব আরোপ করা হয়েছে। সাধারণ আইন-কানুনের মত তা শুধু প্রশাসনের উপর ন্যস্ত করার পরিবর্তে জনসাধারণের মধ্যে আল্লাহ-ভীতির অনুভূতি জাগ্রত করা হয়েছে। বলা হয়েছে যে, যদি ইনসাফ করতে পারবে না বলে মনে কর, তাহলে ইয়াতীম মেয়েদেরকে বিয়ে করবে না; বরং সে ক্ষেত্রে অন্য মেয়েদেরকেই বিয়ে করে নেবে। এ কথা বলার সাথে সাথে সরকারের দায়িত্বশীল ব্যক্তিদের দায়িত্বের কথাও স্মরণ করিয়ে দেয়া হয়েছে। যাতে ইয়াতীম ছেলে-মেয়েদের কোন প্রকার অধিকার ক্ষুণ্ণ না হয় সে ব্যাপারে পুরোপুরি সচেতন থাকার জন্য নির্দেশ দেয়া হয়েছে।
(১) জাহেলিয়াত যুগে ইয়াতীম মেয়েদের অধিকার চরমভাবে ক্ষুণ্ণ করা হতো। যদি কোনো অভিভাবকের অধিনে কোনো ইয়াতীম মেয়ে থাকতো আর তারা যদি সুন্দরী হতো এবং তাদের কিছু সম্পদ-সম্পত্তিও থাকতো, তাহলে তাদের অভিভাবকেরা নামমাত্র মাহর দিয়ে তাদেরকে বিয়ে করে নিত অথবা তাদের সন্তানদের সাথে বিয়ে দিয়ে সম্পত্তি আত্মসাৎ করতো। এইসব অসহায় মেয়েদের পূর্ণ অধিকার সংরক্ষণের কথা তারা চিন্তাও করতো না। আয়েশা সিদ্দিকা (রাঃ) থেকে বর্ণিত আছে যে, মহানবী (সাঃ) এর যুগে ঠিক এই ধরণের একটি ঘটনা সংঘটিত হয়েছিল। জনৈক ব্যক্তির তত্ত্বাবধানে একটি ইয়াতীম মেয়ে ছিল। সে ব্যক্তির একটি বাগান ছিল, যার মধ্যে উক্ত ইয়াতীম বালিকাটিরও অংশ ছিল। সে ব্যক্তি উক্ত মেয়েটিকে বিয়ে করে নিল এবং নিজের পক্ষ থেকে দেনমোহর আদায়তো করলোই না বরং বাগানে মেয়েটির যে অংশ ছিল তাও সে আত্মসাৎ করে নিল। এই ঘটনার পরিপ্রেক্ষিতেই উপরোক্ত আয়াত নাযিল হয় (বুখারী-৪৫৭৩)। অন্য বর্ণনায় এসেছে, আয়েশা (রাঃ) বলেন, তখনকার দিনে কারো কাছে কোনো ইয়াতীম থাকলে এবং তার সম্পদ ও সৌন্দর্য তাকে মুগ্ধ করলে সে তাকে বিয়ে করতে চাইতো। তবে তাকে অন্যদের সমান মাহর দিতে চাইত না। তাই তাদের মাহর পূর্ণ ও সর্বোচ্চ পর্যায়ের না দিয়ে বিয়ে করতে নিষেধ করা হয়েছে। তাদের ব্যাপারে কোনো প্রকার ত্রুটি করার ইচ্ছা তাদের বাদ দিয়ে অন্যান্য মহিলাদের বিয়ে করতে নির্দেশ দেয়া হয়েছে (বুখারী-৪৫৭৪)। তবে এর অর্থ এই নয় যে, অন্যান্য নারীদের বেলায় ইনসাফ বিধান করা লাগবে না। বরং অন্যান্য নারীদের বেলায়ও তা করতে হবে (আত-তাফসীরুস সহীহ)।
(২) বহুবিবাহ প্রথাটি ইসলামপূর্ব যুগেও দুনিয়ার প্রায় সকল ধর্মতেই বৈধ বলে বিবেচিত হতো। আরব/ভারতীয় উপ-মহাদেশ, ইউরোপ, মিশর, বেবিলন প্রভৃতি দেশেই এই প্রথার প্রচলন ছিল। বহুবিবাহের প্রয়োজনীয়তার কথা বর্তমান যুগেও স্বীকৃত। বর্তমান যুগে ইউরোপের একশ্রেণীর চিন্তাবিদ বহুবিবাহ রহিত করার জন্য তাদের অনুসারিদেরকে উদ্বুদ্ধ করে আসছেন বটে কিন্তু তাতে কোনো সুফল হয় নি বরং তাতে সমস্যা আরোও বৃদ্ধি পেয়েছে এবং এর ফল রক্ষিতার রুপে প্রকাশ পেয়েছে। অবশেষে প্রাকৃতিক ও স্বাভাবিক ব্যবস্থারই বিজয় হয়েছে। তাই আজকে ইউরোপের দূরদর্শী চিন্তাশীল ব্যক্তিরা বহু-বিবাহ পুনঃপ্রচলন করার জন্য চিন্তা-ভাবনা করছেন। ইসলাম একই সময়ে চারের অধিক স্ত্রী রাখাকে হারাম ঘোষণা করেছে। ইসলাম এ ক্ষেত্রে ইনসাফ কায়েমের জন্য বিশেষ তাগিদ দিয়েছে এবং ইনসাফের পরিবর্তে যুলুম করা হলে তার জন্য শাস্তির কথা ঘোষণা করেছে। আলোচ্য আয়াতে একাধিক অর্থ্যাৎ চারজন স্ত্রী গ্রহণ করার সুযোগ অবশ্য দেয়া হয়েছে, অন্যদিকে এই চার পর্যন্ত কথাটি আরোপ করে তার উর্ধ সংখ্যক কোনো স্ত্রী গ্রহণ করতে পারবে না বরং তা হবে সম্পূর্ণ নিষিদ্ধ-তাও ব্যক্ত করে দিয়েছে। ইসলাম পূর্ব যুগে কারো কারো দশটি পর্যন্ত স্ত্রী থাকতো। ইসলাম এটাকে চারের মধ্যে সীমাবদ্ধ করে দিয়েছে। কায়েস ইবন হারেস বলেন, 'আমি যখন ইসলাম গ্রহণ করি তখন আমার স্ত্রী সংখ্যা ছিল আট। রাসুলুল্লাহ (সাঃ) এর কাছে আসলে তিনি আমাকে বললেন এর মধ্যে থেকে চারটি গ্রহণ করে নাও। [ইবন মাজাহ ১৯৫২, ১৯৫৩]
(১) পবিত্র কুরআনে চারজন স্ত্রীর কথা বৈধ ঘোষণা করা হয়েছে সাথে সাথে এও বলে দেয়া হয়েছে যে, যদি তোমরা তাদের মধ্যে সমতা বিধান তথা ন্যায় বিচার করতে না পার, তাহলে এক স্ত্রীর উপরই নির্ভর কর। এতে বোঝা যাচ্ছে যে, একাধিক বিয়ে ঠিক তখনই বৈধ হতে পারে, যখন শরী'আত মোতাবেক সবার সাথে সমান আচরণ করা হবে; তাদের সবার অধিকার সমভাবে সংরক্ষণ করা হবে। এ ব্যাপারে অপারগ হলে এক স্ত্রীর উপরই নির্ভর করতে হবে। এবং এটাই ইসলামের নির্দেশ। রাসুল (সাঃ) একাধিক স্ত্রীর বেলায় সবার সাথে পরিপূর্ণ সমতার ব্যবহার করার ব্যাপারে বিশেষ তাগিদ দিয়েছেন এবং যারা এর খেলাফ করবে তাদের জন্য কঠিন শাস্তির খবর দিয়েছেন। নিজের ব্যবহারিক জীবনেও তিনি এ ব্যাপারে সর্বোত্তম আদর্শ স্থাপন করে দেখিয়েছেন। এমনকি তিনি এমন বিষয়ও সমতাপূর্ণ আদর্শ স্থাপন করেছেন যেক্ষেত্রে এর প্রয়োজন ছিল না। এক হাদিসে রাসুল (সাঃ) এরশাদ করেছেনঃ- 'যে ব্যক্তির দুই স্ত্রী রয়েছে সে যদি এদের মধ্যে ব্যবহারের ক্ষেত্রে পূর্ণ সমতা ও ইনসাফ করতে না পারে তবে কিয়ামতের ময়দানে সে এমন ভাবে উঠবে যে, তার শরীরের, এক পার্শ্ব অবশ হয়ে থাকবে। আবু দাউদ ২১৩৩-তিরমিযি ১১৪১, ইবন মাজাহ ১৯৬৯, আহমাদ ২/৪৭১।
এ সূরার ১২৯ নং আয়াতে বলা হয়েছে, কোন এক স্ত্রীর প্রতি যদি তোমার আন্তরিক আকর্ষণ বেশি হয়ে যায়, তবে সেটা তোমার সাধ্যায়ত্ব ব্যাপার নয় বটে, কিন্তু এ ক্ষেত্রেও অন্যজনের প্রতি পরিপূর্ণ উপেক্ষা প্রদর্শন করা জায়েজ হবে না। সূরা আন-নিসার এ আয়াতে ইনসাফপূর্ণ ব্যবহার করতে না পারার আশংকার ক্ষেত্রে এক বিয়েতেই তৃপ্ত থাকার নির্দেশ এবং পরবর্তী আয়াতে 'তোমরা কোনো অবস্থাতেই একাধিক স্ত্রীর মধ্যে সমতা রক্ষা করতে পারবে না। এ দু'আয়াতের মধ্যে সমন্বয় হচ্ছে, এখানে মানুষের সাধ্যায়ত্ব ব্যাপারে স্ত্রীদের মধ্যে সমতা বজায় রাখার কথা বলা হয়েছে। পক্ষ্যান্তরে দ্বিতীয় আয়াতে যা মানুষের সাধ্যর বাইরে অর্থ্যাৎ আন্তরিক আকর্ষণের ব্যাপারে সমতা রক্ষা করা সম্ভব নয় বলে মন্তব্য করা হয়েছে। সুতরাং দু'টি আয়াতে মর্মে যেমন কোনো বৈপরীত্ব নেই, তেমনি এ আয়াতের দ্বারা একাধিক বিবাহের অবৈধতা ও প্রমানিত হয় না। যদি আমরা এ আয়াতের শানে-নুযুলের দিকে দৃষ্টিপাত করি তাহলে ব্যাপারটা আরও স্পষ্ট হয়ে যায়। আয়েশা (রাঃ) বলেছেন, একটি ইয়াতীম মেয়ে এক ব্যক্তির তত্ত্বাবধানে ছিল। লোকটি সে ইয়াতীম মেয়েটির সাথে সম্পদে অংশীদারও ছিল। সে তাকে তার সৌন্দর্য ও সম্পদের জন্য ভালবাসতো। কিন্তু সে তাকে ইনসাফপূর্ণ মাহর দিতে রাজি হচ্ছিল না। তখন আল্লাহ তায়ালা এ আয়াত নাযিল করে মাহর দানের ক্ষেত্রে ইনসাফপূর্ণ ব্যবস্থা কায়েম করার নির্দেশ দেন। ইয়াতীম হলেই তার মাহর কম হয়ে যাবে, এমনটি যেন না হয় সেদিকে গুরুত্বের সাথে লক্ষ্য রাখার নির্দেশ দান করা হয়। [বুখারী ২৪৯৪, ৪৫৭৪, ৫০৯২ মুসলিম: ৩০১৮]। (কোরআনুল কারীম বাংলা অনুবাদ ও সংক্ষিপ্ত তাফসীর) বাদশাহ্ ফাহাদ কোরআন মুদ্রণ কমপ্লেক্স, সৌদিআরব।

20. The sum and substance of the above interpretation is given narrating Sura Annissa Ayat -3. 

21. Thus we see that the Islamic Law permits polygamy. it emphasizes the divine command to "marry only one" where the man fears being unable to fulfill the rights of two or more in a fair manner, so that a substantial segment of the Islamic Scholarship (using ishtehar, independent legal reasoning) argues that it is preferable for man to refrain from multiple marriages in most circumstances. This opinion has codified into the official positions of the Hanbly and Shaafi'i Schools of jurisprudence which asserts that it is which "recommended" (i.e. Mandub, one of the categories of fiqh ruling-Halal, Haram, Wajib, etc.) for a muslim male to have only one wife, even if he may act equitably with more than one women. 

22. In the Hanafi school of thought, as applicable in Bangladesh, polygamy is permissible in Islam, but it is contingent on a man's ability to be just and financially capable of supporting multiple wives. If a man cannot ensure fairness or provide for his wives adequately, polygamy is not advised. This school emphasizes the crucial condition of justice, as outlined in the Quran, and if a man cannot meet these requirements, he should only marry one woman. 

23. Section 255 of Mulla's Principles of Mahomedan Law, Chapter-XIV, deals with Polygamy which runs as follows:—
"255. Number of wives.—A Mahomedan may have as many as four wives at the same time but not more. If he marries a fifth wife when he has already four. the marriage is not void, but merely irregular." 

24. The above quotation recognized polygamy for a Muslim. 

25. Thus in Bangladesh the question of polygamy may be summarized as follows:— 
Permissibility: Polygamy is allowed in Islam, and the Hanafi school accepts it as a permissible practice. 
Core Conditions:—The practice is only allowed if the husband can be fair and financially support multiple wives. 
Requirement for Justice:—The most critical requirement is the ability to be just, which includes providing equal treatment in terms of time, gifts, and other material aspects. 
When Not Recommended:— If a man fears he cannot be fair, he should refrain from polygamy and be content with a single wife, as this is the ideal and better option." 

26. The provision of section 6 does not invalidate also a polygamy (2nd/3rd/4th) marriage which are solemnized having a wife/wives without the permission of the Arbitration Council. The Arbitration Council is very much competent to examine the above ingredients before granting its permission within its power as provided in "6(3) that the proposed marriage is necessary and just"  There is no prohibition to justify the grounds on the Islamic Point of view. Question may arise whether the Arbitration Council is competent to examine the grounds on the Islamic Point of view. As the Muslim marriage is guided by the Principles of Mohamadan Law, the question of polygamy may also be settled in line with the Islamic Principles as stated above. If the Government intends to adopt such a policy, for its implementation, it can do it in any manner for the better interest of the Muslims Citizens of Bangladesh by deleting section 6. Since the rules of Islamic Shariah are applicable in Bangladesh so the Government can give its thought to create an alternative forum in line of section 6 for the personal life of the Muslims of Bangladesh. A different view was found in the following case of Jesinin Sultana vs Md. 11lias reported in 2 BLC (1997) 233 wherein it was held as follows:—
"9. section 6 of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance states that no man, during the subsistence of an existing marriage, shall, except with the previous permission of the Arbitration Council, contracts another marriage. But this section does not declare the second marriage as illegal or invalid, but only prescribes simple imprisonment for one year and fine on conviction for violating the provision of section 6. We therefore, find it necessary to examine the issue as to whether Islam truly approves polygamy or, more properly speaking, polygamy. 10. Since long, we find, there had been great difference of opinion regarding this issue and that arose while interpreting verse 3 of Sure Nisa as hereunder: If your fear that you shall not be able to deal justice with the orphans, marry women of your choice, two, or three, or four; but if you fear that you shall not be able to deal justly, then only one. 12. Thus to be able to deal justly' is the condition precedent to marry more than one woman. Some of the commentators held that the expression implies equality in love and affection, and such equality being impossible in the weakness of human nature, the permission to take another wife amounts virtually to a prohibition. Others took the narrow view and held that equality means only equality in maintenance and lodgment. 17. Polygamy is prohibited in Tunisia under the Law of Personal Status, 1957. According to Tunisian jurists. 'to be able to deal justly' is the injunction legally enforceable and under the modern social and economic conditions this essential condition for polygamy is incapable of fulfillment. So we find that section 6 of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance is against the principle of Islamic law. We recommend that this section be deleted and be substituted with a section prohibiting polygamy. Let a copy of this judgment be sent to the Ministry of Law." 

27. The recommendation of the Hon'ble High Court Division is to delete section 6 of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance, 1961 and to substitute a provision for prohibiting polygamy as it is against the principle of Islamic Law. Instance was given the Country of Tunisia which ban polygamy in 1957. The other Country which ban polygamy is the Turkey. In 1926, Turkey was the first Muslim majority Country to legally ban polygamy. Here in this case also the High Court Division gave emphasized on Islamic Law for deleting section 6 and substituting a new one prohibiting polygamy. The Government still takes no decision in view of the above recommendation. So in view of the above observation a forum, if created by the Government either allowing polygamy from Islamic Point of View or prohibiting polygamy as per recommendation of the High Court Division, may eliminate all the controversies regarding polygamy in Bangladesh. 

28. It is transparent that the process of giving permission of another marriage under section 6 of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance, 1961 is neither discriminatory nor arbitrary. The law does not curtail or take away any right of the parties (both man and women) nor it impose any obstacle upon the Arbitration Council for guaranteeing or refusing permission for polygamy. The Arbitration Council cannot enforce any unilateral decision upon the parties of the marriage. So we do not find any constitutional discrimination in respect of equality and justice as spelt out in the preamble in the constitution as well as equality and discrimination as embodied under Articles 27 and 28 of the Constitution rather the provision is supplement to Article 41 of the Constitution which guarantees the Freedom of Religion subject to law which does not mean that the right to profess, practice and propagate can be taken away by law; it merely means that parliament may by law regulate the manner of professing, practicing and propagating religious believe. As such the argument of constitutional disparity is found absent. There is no tangible interference with religious acts and observances. A long line judicial decisions of the Supreme Court may be found on various aspects of section 6 of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance. 1961 but its applicability questioned only in 2 BLC (1997) 233 deleting section 6 and recognizing Islamic rules of polygamy and framing law against the polygamy limiting only one marriage. In order to constitute a violation of the right of a woman for the cause of polygamy there must be some tangible interference with religious acts and observance. But the petitioner cannot substantiate such grounds before us. In a divorce suit of Christian couple, the High Court Division, while confirming the decree of divorce, made a recommendation that 'a Uniform Marriage and Divorce Act for all the citizens should be enacted by the Parliament keeping in pace with the modern time.' Feeling aggrieved Islamic Law Research Centre and legal Aid Bangladesh filed leave petition. Upon hearing the Appellate Division expunged the recommendation of the High Court Division stating. 'In the background of the provision of Article 41 of the Constitution we are of the view that the said recommendation of the High Court Division taking exception to and against which the leave petition has been filed need be expunged...' (Islamic Law Research Centre and legal Aid Bangladesh vs Eva Chowdhury, (2003) 11 BLT (AD) 180) : 54 DLR (AD) 168. The Appellate Division did not agree with the recommendation of the High Court Division applying Article 41 of the Constitution, It is manifest that freedom of religion is the prime consideration in personal life of the every citizen of Bangladesh irrespective of their religion. It cannot be restricted or taken away in any manner. The Appellate Division in the above cited case observed that the wish of the High Court Division may be implemented by the state. The observation is as follows:— 
"The learned Judges may have their own view as regard particular matter and may 
seriously wish that the same be implemented by the State." 

29. We have also expressed the same view as mentioned above (at page 19). 

30. For the reasons and circumstances discussed above, it is our considered view that section 6 of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance, 1961 does not infringe any fundamental rights of the women citizens of Bangladesh in the process of guaranteeing polygamy. There is thus no substance in the grounds urged in support of the Rule. 

The Rule must accordingly be and is discharged. 

End.

full_judgment:
Abu Bakar Siddiquee, J: This civil appeal, by leave, is directed against the judgment and decree dated the 4th day of February, 2009 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 1499 of 2000 making the Rule absolute. 

2. The facts relevant for disposal of the case are that the respondent as plaintiff instituted Other Class Suit No. 127 of 1995 in the Court of the Assistant Judge, Shibgonj, Bogra praying for a decree for specific performance of contract stating, inter alia, that 2.17 acres land appertaining to CS Khatian No. 24/1, MRR Khatian No. 436, Plot Nos. 35 and 44 of Aushgaon Mouza belonged to defendant No.1 who acquired the same by way of kabala purchase. For payment of debt and also for the purpose of construction of a pucca residence, she gave a proclamation for sale of the suit land through her husband (DW2), The plaintiff offered highest price at Taka 93,000 towards consideration of the said land. Defendant No.1 at the middlemanship of her husband entered into a contract for sale of the suit land. Defendant No.1 received Taka 50,000 in cash through her husband as earnest money and executed an unregistered agreement on 5-5-1995 in favour of the plaintiff. There was stipulation that the rest Taka 43,000 would be paid within 25-8-1995 and defendant No.1 would execute and register the sale deed in favour of the plaintiff. The plaintiff offered the balance money within the said period and requested the defendant to execute and register the kabala deed. The defendant assured the plaintiff that she would execute and register the kabala deed in time, but on 26-8-1995, she refused to execute and register the kabala deed; hence this suit. 

3. Defendant No.1 contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material allegations made in the plaint, contending, inter alia, that it was her specific case that one Rafiqul Islam was the sister's husband. Said Rafiqul Islam on the plea of collection of papers for getting the share of the paternal property of defendant No.1 got her signatures on some blank papers. The plaintiff might have created the bainanama in collusion with said Rafiqul Islam (PW3) using signature as contained in those blank papers and denied to have received any consideration money amounting to Taka 50,000 towards earnest money. She further disclosed in her written statement that she had transferred the suit land by the deed of Hiba-bil-Ewaz dated 22-7-1995 in favour of her brother's son (defendant No.3). 

4. After receiving the copy of the said written statement, the plaintiff amended his plaint and added defendant No. 3 in the plaint and added a prayer seeking for a declaration that the deed of Hiba-bil-Ewaz bearing No. 10417 dated 22-7-1995 executed by defendant No.1 in favour of defendant No. 3 to be declared as collusive, illegal, void and without any consideration and not binding upon the plaintiff. 

5. The learned Assistant Judge framed as many as 4 issues in the suit on consideration of the pleadings of the parties. The plaintiff examined 03 (three) witnesses as PWs while the defendant examined 03(three) witnesses as DWs in support of their respective case. 

6. Upon hearing the parties and on consideration of the materials on record, the learned Assistant Judge, Shibganj, Bogra by his judgment and decree dated 7-10-1998 decreed the suit. 

7. Being aggrieved by the said judgment and decree passed by the learned Assistant Judge, the defendant preferred Other Appeal No. 27 of 1999 before the District Judge, Bogra. The appeal was transferred to the Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Bogra who having heard both the parties allowed the same. 

8. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree passed by the appellate Court, the plaintiff preferred Civil Revision No. 1499 of 2000 before the High Court Division, the learned Judge of the Single Bench of the High Court Division made the Rule absolute. 

9. Against the said judgment and order of the High Court Division, the defendant filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1223 of 2009 and leave was granted to consider the following submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioners:—"Mr. Md. Nawab Ali, learned Advocate-on-Record, appearing for the petitioners submitted that the suit is hit by mis-joinder of cause of action but the High Court Division failed to consider and appreciate the same and thus committed error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice inasmuch as the suit for specific performance of contract and the suit for declaration of title cannot got together but the High Court Division failed to consider the same. The learned Advocate-on-Record further submitted that the issue Nos. HI and IV have been amalgamated with issue No. V though those are separate issues and ought to have been discussed separately but the High Court Division committed error of law in not considering the same." 

10. Mr. Sheikh Mohammad Sirajul Islam, learned Advocate, appearing on behalf of the appellants, submits that the suit is hit by mis-joinder of cause of action, but the High Court Division failed to consider and appreciate the same and thus committed an error of law resulting an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. He further submits that the suit is for specific performance of contract and the suit for declaration of title cannot go together, but the High Court Division failed to consider the same, thus committed an error of law resulting an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. He lastly submits that issue Nos. III and IV have been amalgamated with issue No. V though those are separate issues and ought to have been discussed separately, but the High Court Division committed an error of law in not considering the same. 

11. Mr. Md. Shahidul Islam, learned Advocate, appearing for respondent No.1 made submissions in support of the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division, none appeared on behalf of respondent No. 2 to support the same. 

12. Mr. Md. Shahidul Islam in support of his argument has referred to a decision of our Appellate Division in the Case of Narayan Chandra Das and others vs Jabal Hossain and others reported in 6 MLR (AD) 249 and he submits in the present case since the executants of the bainapatra, i.e. the signature of the executants is proved and admitted by executrix herself there was no reason to disbelieve the bainapatra by the learned Appellate Judge merely on the ground of using of different ink in drawing up of the said bainapatra and putting the signature of the executrix very close to the writing of the bainapatra. In respect of using of different ink, Mr. Islam has referred to a decision of our High Court Division in the case of Sharnim Jahan Chowdhury (Minor) and others reported in 4 BLT 63, he submits that the learned Appellate Judge committed error by finding fault in using different ink by the scribe while writing the said deed of agreement. 

13. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocates for the parties concerned, perused the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division and other connected papers on record. 

14. Admittedly, the suit land belonged to defendant No.1, Hosneara Begum. 

15. The plaintiff-respondent has come with an allegation that defendant-appellant No.1 proposed to sell out the suit land to him and in presence of her husband and the consideration of such suit land was settled at Taka 93,000. It has been further alleged that the husband of defendant No.1 purchased the stamp papers upon which a bainapatra was written and executed by defendant No.1, on receiving Taka 50,000 as an advance out of aforementioned consideration money and thereafter, it has been settled that defendant No.1 would execute and register deed on 25-8-1995 after receiving the balance consideration. It has been also alleged that the plaintiff-respondent tendered the balance consideration within the stipulated period, but defendant No.1 took time to execute and register the deed on various pretext and at last refused to do so on 26-8-1995. It has been further alleged that instead of registering a sale deed in his favour, defendant No.1 subsequently created a Hiba-bil-Ewaz deed in favour of her brother's son on 22-7-1995 and that in presence of earlier bainapatra in his favour, defendant No. 3 acquired no right, title, interest by dint of alleged Hiba-bil-Ewaz. 

16. On the other hand, the plaintiff-respondent denied the aforesaid contention of the plaintiff and counter claimed that she never wanted to sell the suit land to anybody and took no advanced amounting to Taka 50,000 from the plaintiff-respondent and there was no talk of registering any deed as alleged. She further alleged that her husband purchased no stamp paper, but her brother-in-law, namely, Rafiqul Islam obtained her signature on some blank papers on the plea that with a view to effecting partition of her paternal property, it is necessary to collect some documents from the Bagura Collectorate and for such purpose, she had to put her signature on some blank papers. It is admitted by her that she executed a Hiba-bil-Ewaz deed on 22-7-1995 in favour of her brother's son who is enjoying the right, title, interest of the suit land. 

17. It is a settled principle that the plaintiff in order to succeed must establish his own case to obtain a decree and weakness of the defendant's case is no ground for passing a decree in favour of the plaintiff. 

18. Let us proceed to examine the evidence on record and see therefrom as to how far the plaintiff-respondent was able to show the existence of the alleged bainapatra. 

19. The plaintiff-respondent with a view to prove his case has adduced as many as three witnesses as PWs. The plaintiff-respondent while deposing as PW1 stated that defendant No.1 and her husband expressed their willing to sell out the suit land on sitting in their house on 5-5-1995 and the consideration money was fixed on the same day. Whereas PW3, Rafiqul Islam stated that the consideration money and talk of settlement was held in a Friday prior to 5-5-1995. We have already seen from the deposition of PW1 that the fixation of consideration money was held on 5-5-1995 in that case, it is hardly believable that the stamp paper was purchased before that date. PW3 in course of his examination stated that different ink has been used in writing out such bainapatra. Using of such different ink in writing out a bainapatra is very much unusual and impractical and the explanation as has been furnished by PWs 1-3 is quite unusual and unpractical since whenever a scribe is asked to write out a deed, he must input ink in his fountain pen so that he can complete his writing by one pen in a single sitting. PW 3, Rafiqul Islam is a witness to the bainapatra who admitted that he and other witnesses signed the agreement with ball-pen, but the bainapatra itself shows that all the witnesses signed the same with fountain pen using ink. It is the positive case of the plaintiff-respondent that the husband of defendant No.1 was present at the time of talk of settlement and receiving the advanced part of consideration. Thus, it appears that the husband of the defendant is an essential and most important witness. But the husband of the defendant put no signature as an attesting witness of bainapatra. 

20. In this respect, the learned appellate Court below observed in the following verbatim: — 
"বিবাদীনি সুস্পষ্ট ভাবে দাবী করিয়াছেন যে, তাহার ভগ্নিপতি মোঃ রফিকুল ইসলাম পূর্বেই তাহার স্বাক্ষর গ্রহণ করিয়া উহার পরবর্তীতে বায়নাপত্র সৃষ্টি করিয়াছেন।
পি.ডব্লিউ-৩ রফিকুল ইসলামের সাক্ষ্য ও জেরায় যথেষ্ট গরমিল লক্ষ করা যায়। বাদী পক্ষ হইতে দাবী করা হইয়াছে বায়নানামা লেখার সময় কলমের কালী ফুরাইয়া গেলে পুনঃরায় কালী কলমে ভর্তি করিয়া লেখা হয়। কিন্তু প্রদঃ১ পর্যালোচনায় দেখা যায় যে, ডেমীর প্রথম দুই লাইনে এক কালির লেখা তাহার ৩য় লাইনে ভিন্ন কালীর লেখা। অতঃপর পরের ৪ লাইন পূর্বের কালী দ্বারা লেখা। সব শেষের লেখাগুলি পরবর্তীতে কালীর লেখা যায়। অর্থাৎ বিভিন্ন সময় বিভিন্ন কালী ব্যবহার করা হইয়াছে। তর্কিত বায়না নামাপত্রের ৫০ টাকা স্ট্যাম্পে বিবাদী হোসনে আরার একটি স্বাক্ষর রহিয়াছে। উক্ত ষ্ট্যাম্পটি পর্যালোচনা করিলে দেখা যায় যে, প্রথম ৩ লাইন লেখার পরে বেশী কিছু অংশ ফাঁকা রাখা হয়, তাহার পরে পুনঃরায় লেখা শুরু করা হয়। সাধারন লেখার পরে দাতার স্বাক্ষর গ্রহণ করিলে ফাঁকা জায়গার মাঝখানে স্বাক্ষর থাকার কথা। কিন্তু তর্কিত বায়নাপত্রে লেখা যায় লিখিত লেখার লাইনকে প্রায়স্পর্শ করিয়া দাতার স্বাক্ষর লওয়া হইয়াছে। উহা হইতে বুঝা যায় যে, লেখার পূর্বেই দাতার স্বাক্ষর গ্রহণ করা হইয়াছে। ষ্ট্যাম্পও ডেমীতে দাতার সর্বমোট ৩টি স্বাক্ষর রহিয়াছে ঐ ৩টি স্বাক্ষরই বলপেন, যারা করা হইয়াছে। কিন্তু প্রদ:১ এর আর কোথাও বলপেনের লেখা নাই। উহা হইতেই অনুমান করা যায় যে, অদ্য অনুষ্ঠানে বলপেন দ্বারা দাতার স্বাক্ষর লওয়া হইয়াছে। উপরোক্ত বিষয় সমূহ পুংখানুপুংখ ভাবে পর্যালোচনা করিলে দেখা যায় যে, তর্কিত বায়নাপত্রটি পরবর্তীতে সৃষ্টি করা হইয়াছে। যদিও তাহাতে পূর্বেই দাতার স্বাক্ষর গ্রহণ করা হয়।"

21. It is settled principle that a Court of revision under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure can interfere with the findings of fact, as the final Court of facts, only in exceptional circumstances when the findings are shockingly perverse or these are vitiated by non-reading of the material evidence or mis-construction of any important documents affecting the merit of the suit. But in the instant case, we find that the appellate Court below have made a threadbare discussion (as has been quoted aforesaid) and left no stone unturned wherefrom it can be said that there are rooms for mis-appreciation or mis-reading or any scope to non-consideration of evidence on record. 

22. Over and above, the executrix is an illiterate village lady and she can be called as pardanshin in strict sense and in disposition of a deed, section 111 of the Evidence Act case be come into play. The husband of defendant No.1 denied the fact of talk of settlement and receiving Taka 50,000 as an advance while deposing as DW 2. He may be an important witness of bainapatra and also an independent adviser of defendant No.1, but in absence of the signature of DW 2 in the bainapatra as witness, we are not in a position to hold that he was present in the occasion of writing out the same. We hold the view that the High Court Division manifestly erred in law resulting in an error occasioning failure of justice in misreading the evidence on record and failed to consider the legal and admitted facts and in basing decision on mere surmise and conjecture. 

23. In such a state of affairs, it appears from the aforementioned discussion regarding the testimonies of PWs that the plaintiff-respondent has hopelessly failed to prove the fact of existence of such bainapatra. Not only that the High Court Division as a revisional Court has hardly any jurisdiction to set-aside the findings of fact by the appellate Court and that also without discussing any fault in the factual finding by the said Court. 

24. From the discussions made herein before, we find substance in this civil appeal. Accordingly, this appeal is allowed without any order as to costs and the impugned judgment and order dated 4-2-2009 delivered by the High Court Division is set-aside and the judgment and order dated 7-11-1999 passed by the appellate Court below is restored. 

End.
